The *Anāgatavāra* ("Section on the Future", Ya 2.3.3) is an Abhidhamma text belonging to the *Yamaka* collection of the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Like the other analytical chapters of the *Yamaka*, it interrogates canonical doctrinal categories through formalized pairs of questions and answers structured around temporal distinctions—here specifically focusing on the future (*anāgata*) aspect of phenomena [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral]. None of the sampled secondary literature passages discuss this section directly, as occurrences of the keyword *anāgata* in the research corpus refer instead to other texts such as the uncanonical *Anāgatavaṃsa*, the *Anāgatabhayāni* suttas, or generic philosophical uses of the term [DharmaNexus].
Textual reuse analyses generated by DharmaNexus reveal extensive formulaic sharing between the *Anāgatavāra* and other Abhidhamma texts, recording 94 matching passages across 17 Pali works [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments occur with structurally parallel sections of the *Yamaka*, particularly the *Pariññāvāra* (Ya 7.2.4; 23 matches), the *Uppādavāra* (Ya 2.2.1; 15 matches), and other *Anāgatavāra* and temporal sections throughout the collection, such as Ya 10.3.3, Ya 2.3.5, Ya 3.3.1, Ya 3.3.3, and Ya 2.3.2 [DharmaNexus]. Substantial phraseological overlap is also registered with the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi* (Tika Abh09t) and the canonical commentary *Pañcapakaraṇa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus].
